The PAIGC received large quantities of arms from left-leaning African countries. Cuba agreed to supply technicians to the PAIGC. The PAIGC's extension of military control was aided by the jungle-like terrain of Portuguese Guinea. The PAIGC received large quantities of arms from Cuba. The PAIGC received large quantities of arms from China. The PAIGC rapidly extended its military control over large portions of the territory of Portuguese Guinea. Amílcar Cabral was assassinated in January 1973. The PAIGC received large quantities of arms from the Soviet Union. By 1973, the PAIGC was in control of many parts of Guinea. The PAIGC acquired the anti-aircraft capability to defend itself against aerial attack. The African Party for the Independence of Guinea and Cape Verde (PAIGC) was under the leadership of Amílcar Cabral. The PAIGC managed to acquire a significant anti-aircraft capability. The PAIGC's extension of military control was aided by easily reached borderlines with neighbouring allies. The PAIGC movement suffered a setback in January 1973. Cuba agreed to supply artillery experts to the PAIGC. Cuba agreed to supply doctors to the PAIGC.
